elements.requirement: A person (T) is liable to a penalty if T has entered into a transaction involving the making of a supply by or to T and conditions A to C are satisfied.
elements.quote: A person (T) is liable to a penalty where— (a) T has entered into a transaction involving the making of a supply by or to T (“the transaction”), and (b) conditions A to C are satisfied.

elements.requirement: Condition A is satisfied if the transaction was connected with the fraudulent evasion of VAT by another person, whether that evasion occurred before or after T entered into the transaction.
elements.quote: Condition A is that the transaction was connected with the fraudulent evasion of VAT by another person (whether occurring before or after T entered into the transaction).

elements.requirement: Condition B is satisfied if T knew or should have known that the transaction was connected with the fraudulent evasion of VAT by another person.
elements.quote: Condition B is that T knew or should have known that the transaction was connected with the fraudulent evasion of VAT by another person.

elements.requirement: Condition C is satisfied if HMRC have issued a denial decision in relation to the supply that prevents T from exercising or relying on a VAT right in relation to the supply, is based on the facts satisfying conditions A and B, and applies a relevant principle of EU case law regardless of whether the circumstances are identical to those in the relevant European Court of Justice case.
elements.quote: Condition C is that HMRC have issued a decision (“the denial decision”) in relation to the supply which— (a) prevents T from exercising or relying on a VAT right in relation to the supply, (b) is based on the facts which satisfy conditions A and B in relation to the transaction, and (c) applies a relevant principle of EU case law

elements.requirement: A VAT right includes the right to deduct input tax, the right to apply a zero rate to international supplies, and any other right connected with VAT in relation to a supply.
elements.quote: In this section “VAT right” includes the right to deduct input tax, the right to apply a zero rate to international supplies and any other right connected with VAT in relation to a supply.

elements.requirement: The relevant principles of EU case law comprise the principles established by the European Court of Justice in joined Cases C-439/04 and C-440/04 Axel Kittel and Belgium v. Recolta Recycling, Case C-273/11 Mecsek-Gabona Kft, or any other European Court of Justice cases concerning the denial or refusal of a VAT right to prevent abuses of the VAT system decided before section 42 of TCTA 2018 came into force.
elements.quote: The relevant principles of EU case law for the purposes of this section are the principles established by the European Court of Justice in the following cases— (a) joined Cases C-439/04 and C-440/04 Axel Kittel v. Belgian State; Belgium v. Recolta Recycling (denial of right to deduct input tax), and (b) Case C-273/11 (b)Mecsek-Gabona Kft v Nemzeti Adó- és Vámhivatal Dél-dunántúli Regionális Adó Főigazgatósága (denial of right to zero rate), as developed or extended by that Court in any other cases relating to the denial or refusal of a VAT right in order to prevent abuses of the VAT system which were decided before the coming into force of section 42 of TCTA 2018.

elements.requirement: The penalty payable by T under section 69C is 30% of the potential lost VAT.
elements.quote: The penalty payable under this section is 30% of the potential lost VAT.

elements.requirement: Potential lost VAT includes the additional VAT that becomes payable by T as a result of HMRC's denial decision.
elements.quote: the additional VAT which becomes payable by T as a result of the denial decision

elements.requirement: Potential lost VAT includes the VAT that is not repaid to T as a result of HMRC's denial decision.
elements.quote: the VAT which is not repaid to T as a result of that decision

elements.requirement: Potential lost VAT is the aggregate of the VAT not repaid and the additional VAT if, as a result of HMRC's denial decision, VAT is not repaid to T and additional VAT becomes payable by T.
elements.quote: in a case where as a result of that decision VAT is not repaid to T and additional VAT becomes payable by T, the aggregate of the VAT that is not repaid and the additional VAT.

elements.requirement: Where T is liable to a penalty under section 69C, the Commissioners may assess the amount of the penalty and notify it to T.
elements.quote: Where T is liable to a penalty under this section the Commissioners may assess the amount of the penalty and notify it to T accordingly.

elements.requirement: The Commissioners are prohibited from making an assessment of a penalty under section 69C more than two years after the denial decision is issued.
elements.quote: No assessment of a penalty under this section may be made more than two years after the denial decision is issued.

elements.requirement: The assessment of a penalty against T under section 69C may be made immediately after the denial decision is made, and notice of the assessment may be given to T within the same document as the notice of the denial decision.
elements.quote: The assessment of a penalty under this section may be made immediately after the denial decision is made (and notice of the assessment may be given to T in the same document as the notice of the decision).

elements.requirement: Actions taken by T in claiming to exercise or rely on a VAT right do not give rise to liability to a penalty under section 69C if T is assessed for an inaccuracy penalty under paragraph 1 of Schedule 24 to the Finance Act 2007 by reason of those actions and that assessment has not been withdrawn or successfully appealed.
elements.quote: Where by reason of actions involved in making a claim to exercise or rely on a VAT right in relation to a supply T— (a) is liable to a penalty for an inaccuracy under paragraph 1 of Schedule 24 to the Finance Act 2007 for which T has been assessed (and the assessment has not been successfully appealed against by T or withdrawn)

elements.requirement: Actions taken by T in claiming to exercise or rely on a VAT right do not give rise to liability to a penalty under section 69C if T is convicted of an offence, whether under the Value Added Tax Act 1994 or otherwise, by reason of those actions.
elements.quote: Where by reason of actions involved in making a claim to exercise or rely on a VAT right in relation to a supply T— (b) is convicted of an offence (whether under this Act or otherwise), those actions do not give rise to liability to a penalty under this section.
